title: Cylindrical base
spec: Start by creating a new coordinate system with Euler angles set to zero degrees for all axes and a translation vector of [0.2307, 0.2645, 0.0]. On the first face, draw a single circle in the first loop. Position the center of this circle at [0.1105, 0.1105] and set its radius to 0.1105. Apply a scaling factor of 0.2211 to the entire 2D sketch. Rotate the scaled sketch using the Euler angles [0.0, 0.0, 0.0] degrees and translate it using the vector [0.2307, 0.2645, 0.0]. Extrude the sketch along the normal direction by 0.0084 units, ensuring no extrusion in the opposite direction. This extrusion will create a new solid body. The final dimensions of the cylindrical base are 0.22108208955223857 units in length and width, and 0.008395522388059693 units in height.

reference.label: Reference (dataset)
reference.code:
import cadquery as cq

# Define the initial coordinate system transformation
translation_vector = (0.2307, 0.2645, 0.0)
euler_angles = (0.0, 0.0, 0.0)

# Create the sketch for the circular face
circle_center = (0.1105, 0.1105)
circle_radius = 0.1105

# Create the sketch
sketch = cq.Workplane("XY").center(*circle_center).circle(circle_radius)

# Extrude the sketch to create the cylindrical object
extrude_depth_towards_normal = 0.0084
extrude_depth_opposite_normal = 0.0
sketch_scale = 0.2211

# Perform the extrusion
cylinder = sketch.extrude(extrude_depth_towards_normal - extrude_depth_opposite_normal)

# Apply the coordinate system transformation
cylinder = cylinder.translate(translation_vector).rotate((0, 0, 0), (1, 0, 0), euler_angles[0]) \
                         .rotate((0, 0, 0), (0, 1, 0), euler_angles[1]) \
                         .rotate((0, 0, 0), (0, 0, 1), euler_angles[2])

# Final model
r = cylinder
